match.reason: The closest bank point, sci-sexual-asexual-reproduction, covers the identical-offspring versus varied-offspring idea, but the new brief also teaches speed and how variation helps a species survive change, which that card does not cover; the survival idea sits in a separate bank point, so the new point is broader than any single match.

draft.title: Sexual and asexual reproduction
card: One parent makes offspring on its own. The offspring are genetically identical to the parent, and they can be made quickly.
Cells from two parents join to make offspring. Each offspring gets a mix of genes from both parents, so offspring differ from each other and from the parents.

Asexual reproduction works well in a stable environment, because an organism that suits its surroundings has offspring that suit them too. A disease or a change in conditions can harm all identical individuals at once.
Variation from sexual reproduction means some individuals may survive when conditions change. This helps a species continue over time.
draft.remember: Asexual: one parent, identical offspring, fast. Sexual: two parents, varied offspring.

a.q: Which pair correctly describes the offspring of each type of reproduction?
opts: Asexual: identical to the parent. Sexual: varied
Asexual: varied. Sexual: identical to the parent
Both types: identical to the parent
Both types: varied, with genes from two parents
a.why: One parent passes on all its genes in asexual reproduction, so offspring are identical to it. Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents, so offspring vary. The reversed option swaps the two types.
a.clue: Think about how many parents give genes in each type.

b.q: A disease spreads through a farm of identical banana plants grown from cuttings of one parent plant. Why might every plant be harmed?
opts: They are genetically identical, so none may resist it
They were made by two parents, so they all share flaws
They have too much variation to cope with disease
They reproduce too slowly to replace the lost plants
b.why: Cuttings are asexual reproduction, so all the plants are genetically identical. If one cannot resist the disease, none of them may. Slow reproduction is wrong, because asexual reproduction can be quick.
b.clue: Cuttings come from one parent plant.

a.best: Asexual: identical to the parent. Sexual: varied

b.best: They are genetically identical, so none may resist it
